results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT round((sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * l.quantity) / nullif(sum((l.unit_price * l.quantity - l.line_discount) / 1.1), 0)) * 100, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_pct FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32% across the data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. This calculation is based on non-voided orders, using revenue excluding GST minus the cost of the items sold. Please note that this figure excludes any product variants where the cost was missing from the system.
results.assumptions: Calculated overall gross profit margin across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) for non-voided orders. Revenue is ex-GST (revenue divided by 1.1) minus ex-GST variant cost multiplied by quantity. Variants with NULL cost are excluded.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?
results.sql:
WITH gross AS (
  SELECT sum(total) AS gross_revenue
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
), total_refunds AS (
  SELECT sum(amount) AS refund_amount
  FROM refunds r
  JOIN orders o USING (order_id)
  WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
)
SELECT 
  round(gross_revenue, 2) AS gross_revenue,
  round(refund_amount, 2) AS total_refunds,
  round(gross_revenue - refund_amount, 2) AS net_revenue
FROM gross, total_refunds
results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds for the period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026, is $3,205,298.79. This was calculated by taking the gross order revenue of $3,321,930.71 and subtracting $116,631.92 in total refunds. This figure excludes voided orders, assuming all remaining transactions were successfully fulfilled.
results.assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total order revenue (excluding voided orders) minus total refund amounts across the entire dataset period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What percentage of orders had a refund?
results.sql:
WITH order_stats AS ( 
  SELECT 
    COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders, 
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) FILTER (WHERE r.refund_id IS NOT NULL) AS refunded_orders 
  FROM orders o 
  LEFT JOIN refunds r USING (order_id) 
  WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
)
SELECT 
  total_orders, 
  refunded_orders, 
  ROUND(100.0 * refunded_orders / NULLIF(total_orders, 0), 2) AS percentage_with_refund 
FROM order_stats;
results.answer: Out of your 17,340 total orders, 5.7% had a refund, which equals 988 refunded orders. This covers the entire data period from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026, and excludes any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Calculated the percentage of non-voided orders that have at least one associated refund record across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'YYYY-MM') AS month, round(sum(orders.total)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue FROM orders WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' AND orders.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= (TIMESTAMP '2026-09-30' - INTERVAL '3 months') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
results.answer: Your gross revenue across the last 3 complete months (June to August 2026) was $13,835.62 in June, $342,251.10 in July, and $282,129.97 in August. Note that this data covers non-voided orders and also includes an extra row for September 2026 that was returned in the results.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months? Date range covers June 2026 to August 2026 (the 3 complete calendar months preceding today, 2026-09-30). Revenue is gross revenue (orders.total) for non-voided orders.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'EOFY Sale' AS period,
    sum(total) AS gross_revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date BETWEEN '2026-06-19' AND '2026-07-05'
),
pre_eofy_period AS (
  SELECT 
    'Pre-EOFY (17 days)' AS period,
    sum(total) AS gross_revenue,
    count(order_id) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date BETWEEN '2026-06-02' AND '2026-06-18'
)
SELECT period, round(gross_revenue, 2) AS gross_revenue, order_count FROM eofy_period
UNION ALL
SELECT period, round(gross_revenue, 2) AS gross_revenue, order_count FROM pre_eofy_period;
results.answer: Revenue increased during the EOFY sale, rising to $246,002.91 across 1,240 orders compared to $186,171.83 from 794 orders in the preceding 17 days. This comparison assumes we are looking at the 17-day EOFY sale period against the exact same number of days immediately prior, while excluding any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Comparing gross revenue and order counts between the EOFY sale period (19 June to 5 July 2026, 17 days) and the immediately preceding 17 days (2 June to 18 June 2026). Excluded voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title AS product_title, sum(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v USING (product_id) JOIN order_lines l USING (variant_id) JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC LIMIT 3
results.answer: The three products that sold the fewest units across the entire data period are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These figures exclude voided orders and group products by their title.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), excluding voided orders? Products are grouped by title.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND customer_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id HAVING count(DISTINCT order_id) >= 3) t
results.answer: There are 1,640 unique customers who have placed three or more orders. This count excludes guest checkouts because they cannot be grouped as a single customer.
results.assumptions: Counting unique customers with 3 or more non-voided orders. Guest checkouts (customer_id IS NULL) are excluded since they cannot be grouped as a single customer.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS average_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after the order date. This is calculated using the time difference between when an order is placed and when the refund is processed.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued across all refund events, based on the difference between refund timestamp and order timestamp.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS total_discounted_revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND discount_id IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Orders that used a discount brought in $944,363.46 in gross revenue. This total covers all non-voided orders from October 1, 2025, through September 30, 2026.
results.assumptions: Interpreting revenue as gross revenue (orders.total) for non-voided orders that have a non-null discount_id, covering the entire date range of the data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color AS colour, SUM(l.quantity) AS units_sold FROM order_lines l JOIN orders o ON l.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON l.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY units_sold DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: Camel was your top-selling colour in winter 2026, with a total of 1050 units sold. This result is based on completed orders between June 1 and August 31, 2026, excluding any voided transactions.
results.assumptions: Interpreting winter 2026 as June 1, 2026 to August 31, 2026 in Australia/Sydney time, excluding voided orders.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, ROUND(SUM(o.total)::numeric, 2) AS gross_revenue, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: Your weekdays brought in more money than your weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 across 6,187 orders on weekends. This covers all your available data from October 2025 through September 2026. Keep in mind that weekdays outnumber weekends, which naturally drives up the total weekday revenue.
results.assumptions: Interpreting as: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue for all available data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is gross revenue (orders.total) excluding voided orders, attributed to Australia/Sydney local time.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT count(*) AS order_count FROM (SELECT o.order_id FROM orders o JOIN order_lines l ON o.order_id = l.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING sum(l.quantity) > 1) t
results.answer: There were 8,908 non-voided orders that contained more than one unit in total. This count is based on orders where the sum of quantities across all order lines is greater than one.
results.assumptions: Counting non-voided orders where the sum of quantities across all order lines is greater than one.

results.question: For each store location show the number of orders, units sold and revenue
results.sql: WITH order_stats AS (    SELECT      l.location_id,      l.name AS store_location,      count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS number_of_orders,      round(sum(o.total), 2) AS gross_revenue    FROM locations l    JOIN orders o ON l.location_id = o.location_id    WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'    GROUP BY l.location_id, l.name), line_stats AS (    SELECT      l.location_id,      sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold    FROM locations l    JOIN orders o ON l.location_id = o.location_id    JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id    WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'    GROUP BY l.location_id) SELECT   os.store_location,   os.number_of_orders,   COALESCE(ls.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold,   os.gross_revenue FROM order_stats os LEFT JOIN line_stats ls ON os.location_id = ls.location_id ORDER BY os.gross_revenue DESC;
results.answer: The Online Store generated the most revenue with $2,070,833.88 across 10,667 orders and 20,372 units sold, followed by Surry Hills Boutique with $755,981.28 from 4,036 orders and 7,533 units, and Newtown Boutique with $495,115.55 from 2,637 orders and 4,966 units. These figures represent gross revenue and separate order counts from order lines to prevent inflating the totals.
results.assumptions: Computed order counts and gross revenue from orders grouped by location separately from units sold via order_lines to avoid inflating order totals.
